want.who_she_is: Nell Vasey, 19. She was supposed to leave in September; the money wasn't there, so she didn't, and the gap year is quietly becoming her life. She has never lived anywhere else — her room is the room she was eight in. One bathroom, five adults. Her father takes board off everyone in the house, £50 a week, Sunday night, cash, at the kitchen table, because everyone contributes. Her Saturday shift on the parade pays £36. The gap is covered by an allowance she has to ask for out loud, itemised, in front of whoever is in the kitchen. What she has to lose is nothing dramatic, and that is the point: the only number anyone has ever put on Nell Vasey is the one on the back of her father's envelope, and everyone in the house has seen it.
want.appetite: To be wanted by the people who set her price — and to keep the number moving. It cannot complete: no figure settles it, and the moment one is agreed she wants the next one set by someone else. Release 41 adds a new relative in the box room, a new thing in the house that turns out to have a price, or another rung on someone already at that table.
want.ascent: Bottom: she asks, itemises, waits for the bathroom, and knocks on every door in the house including her own, because the catch is loud and her mother sleeps in the afternoons. Top: she names the number and the table pays it — the Sunday envelope runs the other way, no room needs an invitation, no door is waited outside, nothing she wants has to be justified. Four ratcheting tiers plus a counterweight: NERVE (how far she'll go with blood), SEEN (how much she lets herself be looked at in a house with no locks), PRICE (what she'll take money for and how openly), APPETITE (what she wants for its own sake — and at its ceiling the game stops offering and starts firing), against STANDING (what the house thinks she is, spent by every ask, buys nothing).
want.charge_note: Blood the whole way — father, brother, uncle, mother. No step, no patch, no asterisk. The reversal is mechanical and it is why this is a game rather than a scene: the kitchen table is a pricing mechanism that exists to decide what Nell is owed and what Nell owes, once a week, in public, in front of her family. The ascent is her learning to move other things across that same table until the direction of the money reverses.
want.appetite_is_not_arousal: APPETITE is a ratchet — the standing baseline of what she needs before anything happens that day. Arousal is volatile layer-2 weather and must never be conflated with it.

why_this_person.npc_martin: Her father, 52. The ledger. Not cruel and never has been — procedural, which is worse: every fifteen pounds gets a follow-up question, asked kindly, in front of everyone. He decides what she is worth, weekly, in cash. To be wanted by the auditor is to break the audit.
why_this_person.npc_joss: Her brother, 22. Nights at the depot, sleeps days, never left either. Room opposite hers; their windows share the flat roof over the kitchen. He noticed first and he is the only person in the house who will say a price out loud. Not harmless, not nervous — practical. The fastest rung, and the one who could end her at any moment by saying it at dinner.
why_this_person.npc_denise: Her mother, 49. Nights at the care home, home at half six, asleep by eight. In the house for the whole game and the only person who could stop it. For seventy-four rungs she is the risk surface — the reason doors get closed and the reason they get left open. At seventy-five she is the rung.
why_this_person.npc_gareth: Her uncle, 45 — Martin's younger brother, in the box room since the divorce, putting a bit toward things. The second man with an opinion on her allowance and no standing to have one. Also the first occupant of a slot that never empties.
why_this_person.npc_col: 41, runs the shop on the parade where she does Saturdays. The only money that is not the allowance and the only man who is not family. He is what an honest price looks like, which is what makes the household's prices legible as what they are.

rotating_slot.rule: The Vaseys take in whichever relative is between things — Gareth now, a cousin next, an aunt after. The renewable character slot, renewable IN BLOOD, so the taboo does not reset when the occupant does. Room-scoped content (the room, the shared wall, the arrangement) lives in 3_activities.toml and names the occupant by ROLE only; tenant-scoped content (his ladder, his register, his props, his one secret) lives in 5_scenes.toml and dies with him.

throttle_plan.doctrine: the-meters.md M1-M5. Every rung that grants an ascent tier carries TWO brakes.
throttle_plan.brake_a: `costs` on the hub choice — energy 8-15. Engine-enforced: an unaffordable choice is not offered (engine.md §27).
throttle_plan.brake_b: a `<rung>_today` FLAG set on the rung's exit and gated `is_false` on the hub choice, cleared in [engine.daily_tick]. A flag, never a counter trait — a player-subject trait read only by `lt` reads to gate 10 as a descent (the-meters.md M5).
throttle_plan.brake_c: presence. Every family rung needs its person on site, and each is on site 2-4 hours a day.
throttle_plan.spacing: +2 to +4 per rung against thresholds at 15/35/55/75
throttle_plan.target_rate: fastest route to a top band 8-11 in-game days (M2 target: 7-10)
throttle_plan.cap_note: M6 — `cap` never goes on an ascent tier. Restores only (energy on sleep, hygiene on a wash).

sidebar_plan.money: trait_bar, hide_value = false, NO bands — a countable resource is never banded
sidebar_plan.top_band_rule: leave the top band's max off, or cap the terminal add — a value outside every band renders nothing at all (engine.md §30)

The occupancy engine. One bathroom, five adults, and a bolt that turns without catching. Contention, waiting, and being walked in on are all the same mechanic here.
Her base, and the room she was eight in. The afternoon room — mother asleep down the hall, Joss awake across the landing.

decisions.note: Premise chosen from a study of the four female-protagonist games in the mopoga top-30 (Zara's School Life, New Life Project, Family Ties, Cupid's Way) plus DoL. Two findings drove it: (1) every incest game in the top-30 is male-POV — the daughter/sister POV exists only as a subsystem under someone else's goal, which is the open lane; (2) all four fem-protag entries run ONE global corruption master-gate and all four generate stat-wall/cheat revolt, while the only fem-capable entry running split ratcheting tiers (DoL) has 6 grind complaints in 1,267. So: Zara's validated shape — 'as her corruption rises the gameplay expands' — on DoL's four-tier structure.

`appetite` as a forcing tier is lifted from Cupid's Way's `$bbc_addict >= 5`, which FORCES content rather than offering it. It is the one female-protagonist mechanic nobody else in the studied set ships, and it makes the top of an ascent feel like a loss of choice rather than a bigger menu.

Deliberately differentiated from `back_home`, the other domestic v2 game. Held on purpose: blood family not step; she NEVER left rather than returned; the mother is present, awake and is the ceiling rather than absent; the anchor is a table that prices things rather than a room the house collects in; money is the master verb (charged board + itemised allowance in one closed loop) rather than a side system; the renewable box-room slot is a relative rather than a lodger; tiers are nerve/seen/price/appetite rather than nerve/exposure/need.

Nine locations, derived rather than picked: seven rooms the cast's rotas actually visit plus the exterior the map owes (the-map.md R3) plus the one workplace that is the non-household income. the_back_bedroom ships LOCKED — it is simultaneously the release-closing door (gate 9) and the room the Want owes at nerve 75 (the-map.md R2), so declaring it now costs 300 words and prevents the measured failure where a promised room was never built.

The kitchen is the anchor at 30% of plan because this terrace has no separate lounge — a design choice, not an accident. The room the house lives in and the room that prices things are the same room, which is the entire premise expressed as a floor plan.

Brakes designed BEFORE the prose, per the-meters.md M1-M5 — the measured failure was a game with three correctly-gated tiers, zero brakes, and every tier topped out inside two in-game days. Every rung carries `costs` energy AND a `_today` flag cleared in [engine.daily_tick], and a flag rather than a counter trait specifically so gate 10 does not read the brake as a descent.

Board is charged by [settings.rent], not by an authored canvas. This is the direct lesson of the measured forty_miles defect where the game's title mechanic was narrated in prose and never took a penny; per the-economy.md R3 the authored scenes sit beside the charge, never on it.

joss_room re-planned 1,100 -> 1,400 words. NOT a back-fill: gate 22 requires every declared object to be written AND to afford a choice, and `his bed` had neither, so the room owed a real standing surface that the board's first count did not know about. Logged rather than silently widened, because a budget that moves without a reason is the post-hoc record the-board.md refuses to credit.

Gate 22 changed the shape of every room. The first pass wrote each location's affordances as separate activity canvases whose exits were type="location", so no room had a CHOICE hanging off a declared object and 35 of 39 objects were texture. Fixed by giving each location a room screen: the paragraph names the things, every choice hangs off one of them, and the count falls out of the objects (6 in the kitchen, 3 in the back bedroom). the-surfaces.md R2b.

Gate 18 resolves brakes PER ROUTE INTO A CANVAS, so a money grant on a node inside a room screen reads as free income — the route in is the location menu, which costs nothing. The price-75 reversal was therefore split into its own triggerless rung (rung_kitchen_reversal) with the brake on the referring choice. Node-level grants inside a multi-node screen are invisible to the economy gates.
Every thought_bubble shipped without props.speaker in the first pass — 22 of them. A missing speaker renders as the literal 'Npc' (v2.py:14631); it is never a default. Fixed game-wide.
